Manage and refer urgently:
Sit patient up and if oxygen saturation < 94%, give 40% face mask oxygen at 6-8L/min.
If systolic BP > 90, give furosemide 40mg slow IV. If no response after 30 minutes, give another 80mg IV. If good response, give 40mg IV after 2-4 hours.
If systolic BP > 90, give sublingual isosorbide dinitrate 5mg even if there is no chest pain. Repeat every 10 minutes if SBP remains >90.
If BP ≥ 180/130, give single dose enalapril 10mg orally.
HEART FAILURE: ROUTINE CARE
The patient with heart failure has leg swelling and difficulty breathing which worsens on lying down/with effort. A doctor must confirm the diagnosis and refer the patient for specialist assessment.

Advise the patient with heart failure • Advise to adhere to treatment even if asymptomatic. Advise to avoid NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen). Advise regular exercise within limits of symptoms. Help patient to manage CVD risk 144. • Advise to restrict salt to < half a teaspoon/day and fluids to 1.5L/day (6 cups). If possible, advise to monitor weight daily. If patient gains ≥ 2kg in 2 days, advise to return to clinic.

1One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer. 2If ECG shows heart block or bradyarrhythmias, refer. 3If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely.
Assess the patient with heart failure
Assess When to assess Note
Symptoms Every visit Manage symptoms as on symptom pages. If fainting/blackouts, refer same day.
Family planning Every visit Assess patient's contraceptive needs 170. If pregnant or planning pregnancy, refer for specialist care.
Substance use Every visit In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks1/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription/over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165.
Weight Every visit Assess changes in fluid balance by comparing with weight when patient least symptomatic.
BP and pulse Every visit If known hypertension 149. If not known hypertension and BP ≥ 140/90 148. If new irregular pulse, refer same day.
Palliative care Every visit Assess need for palliative care 191.
Creatinine (eGFR) and potassium

At diagnosis, 6 monthly • If starting/increasing dose of enalapril/spironolactone: also check after 2 weeks if eGFR < 60, or after 4 weeks if eGFR ≥ 60. • If creatinine increases by > 20%, eGFR < 30 or potassium > 5.0, stop enalapril/spironolactone and discuss with specialist.
Other blood tests At diagnosis Test for HIV 124. Check Hb, TSH and if not known diabetes, check fingerprick glucose 19. If abnormal, discuss with specialist.

Treat the patient with heart failure • Give influenza vaccine 0.5mL IM yearly. Aim to have patient on steps 1 and 2. Add step 3 if patient has ongoing symptoms on steps 1 and 2. If uncontrolled on steps 1-3, refer to specialist for digoxin. Medication Dose Note
Hydrochlorothiazide or furosemide and enalapril
25-50mg daily For mild heart failure. Avoid if: eGFR < 30, liver disease, gout, pregnancy. Use cautiously if personal/family history of skin cancer.
Start 40mg daily. If needed, increase every 2-3 days until symptoms improve, up to 250mg/day.
• Use if severe heart failure symptoms or eGFR < 60. Once improved, consider switch to HCTZ if eGFR ≥ 60. • If > 80mg needed, give half dose 12 hourly.
Start 2.5mg 12 hourly. If needed, increase up to 10mg 12 hourly. Avoid if pregnant, previous angioedema, aortic stenosis, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, renal artery stenosis.

2 Add carvedilol Start 3.125mg 12 hourly. If tolerated, double dose every 2 weeks until symptoms improve, up to 25mg 12 hourly. • Start once on optimal dose of enalapril and aim for resting pulse 50-70. • If > 85 kg, titrate to a maximum of 50mg twice daily, if tolerated. If still symptomatic, do ECG2 and/or refer. • Avoid if severe fluid overload, cardiogenic shock3, BP < 90/60, asthma. Avoid or decrease dose if pulse < 50.
3 Add spironolactone 25mg daily Monitor potassium and kidney function. Avoid if eGFR < 30 or potassium > 5.0. Stop potassium supplements.
